# Worker supervisor

The script runs each job in jobs.txt with at most four workers and writes one log per job.

~~~bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

readonly JOBS_FILE="jobs.txt"
readonly LOG_DIR="logs"
readonly MAX_PARALLEL=4
readonly JOB_TIMEOUT=30

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

pids=()
running=0
status=0

cleanup() {
    local code=$?
    trap - TERM INT
    for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do
        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
    wait 2>/dev/null || true
    exit "$code"
}
trap cleanup TERM INT

run_job() {
    local job_id=$1
    local log="$LOG_DIR/$job_id.log"
    printf '%s started\n' "$job_id"
    exec timeout -k 2 "$JOB_TIMEOUT" ./worker.sh "$job_id" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1 3<&-
}

exec 3<"$JOBS_FILE"
while IFS= read -r job_id <&3; do
    if [ -z "$job_id" ]; then
        continue
    fi
    while [ "$running" -ge "$MAX_PARALLEL" ]; do
        if ! wait -n; then
            status=1
        fi
        running=$((running - 1))
    done
    run_job "$job_id" &
    pids+=("$!")
    running=$((running + 1))
done
exec 3<&-

while [ "$running" -gt 0 ]; do
    if ! wait -n; then
        status=1
    fi
    running=$((running - 1))
done

exit "$status"
~~~

## Process model

Each worker is a separate process with its own virtual address space and file descriptor table. Threads would share that address space; separate processes contain a crash and let the deadline end one job without touching the others.

The supervisor opens the job list on descriptor 3 so a worker cannot consume the list from stdin, and closes descriptor 3 in the child so the open file does not outlive the loop. Each job runs under timeout -k, which sends SIGTERM at the deadline and SIGKILL two seconds later because SIGKILL cannot be caught. The trap forwards SIGTERM to every running job, wait -n reaps each child so no zombie is left behind, and any nonzero status makes the supervisor exit nonzero.
